Before anything else- do not treat this as a free game. It costs roughly $4. Unless you spend $4, multiple features are locked behind watching ads, and the game is unplayable. $4 removes all ads permanently. ---------------- This is a fun little game. I've been playing it on my phone for a few months, I'm glad to see it get on PC. To start with the TL;DR, the game isn't perfect or anything. There's a good chunk of microtransactions, and the game is currently a bit on the easy side with the exception of 2 specific super-bosses. The core gameplay is really fun though, there's more customization here than probably any rougelite I've played. The pixel are is fantastic too. But aside from that, the game is a good time. It won't blow your mind, but I don't think it's trying to. It's a fun Rougelite with lots of characters, each having different weapons you can use and skill trees to mess with before the run even begins, giving tons of customizability to how you can play. The characters are fun and unique too, with newer weapons making the older 'outdated' characters get a fresh feel. Despite lots of stuff you can spend real money on in the shop, the regular progression speed of the game is quite good, until you've bought all but the last 6 characters or so, then it starts to become a grind. Fortunately, the process of simply playing the game is fun. Finally, the PC client runs really well. The game mostly feels good on controller, with the only strange feel being trying to jump diagonally while holding attack- something easy on phone but strangely awkward feeling on controller for some reason. The shop is also in Korean currency on PC for some reason, which is pretty funny. It'll probably be patched, the dev is pretty fast at updating the game in general. My only other complaint is that the audio quality feels pretty low. It wasn't great on the phone already, and it feels a bit worse here. It isn't awful, but it's not great. Sound Effects are too loud on both versions, I'd recommend turning them down about 15 points below music. Anyway. Fun little game. It's a good time, and I hope it continues to grow.

i have been unfair.. while unfortunately, my original comment >>> "has a replicable 100% chance to CTD in arena mode (enter the mimic after 1st round & go right). how long has this game been out? yea..." <<< still holds true and renders arena mode unplayable until they fix it, i'm gonna do something i haven't really felt the need for in a long time: change my review from negative to positive. not really near end-game yet, tho i've enjoyed coming back to it several times now, played the starting character to lvl30 and tried out 3 other ones. there is lots of stuff to unlock, a good variety of builds, synergies and itemisation to play around with. grinding for the resources has mostly been enjoyable so far, but it's important to mention that i can't judge endgame progression yet and for that i reserve judgement. imho, calling it mobile slop is a cheap shot and not genuinely fair. yes, it is bad that you can't bind controls to mouse buttons and while i have no idea if they plan to change that, i can only speak for myself insofar that having bound the attack and special attack buttons to 2 keys on the numpad instead of LMB & RMB has been perfectly fine and i don't even think about wanting mouse controls in it anymore. it doesn't cost money to try out, so if you are interested in the genre, i'd recommend you give it a shot and see for yourself if it's your cup of tea.

Developed and published by 96Percent, DUNGEON SLASHER is a side-scrolling roguelike action game that thrives on speed, experimentation, and repeatability. Built around the idea that no two dungeon runs should feel exactly alike, it places players in a relentless cycle of battling monsters, gathering powerful upgrades, and pushing deeper into increasingly dangerous environments. Its pixel-art presentation immediately captures the spirit of classic arcade adventures, but beneath the nostalgic visuals lies a modern progression system designed to keep players invested over dozens of hours. The game's biggest strength is the flexibility it offers through its extensive collection of heroes, abilities, and artifacts. Every run presents a new opportunity to create wildly different playstyles. Players can lean into aggressive melee builds, prioritize mobility and evasive tactics, or assemble combinations that flood the screen with devastating special attacks. This variety transforms the familiar roguelike formula into an engaging sandbox of experimentation. Even failed attempts contribute to the experience, as players gradually unlock new options and gain a better understanding of which synergies are worth pursuing. Combat remains the centerpiece throughout the adventure. Enemies attack from all directions, requiring quick reactions and constant movement to survive. The controls are easy to pick up, allowing newcomers to jump into the action without much friction, but mastering the timing of dodges, skill usage, and positioning becomes increasingly important as the difficulty escalates. Boss encounters are particularly memorable, demanding a balance of mechanical skill and strategic preparation. These battles serve as effective milestones that break up the routine of standard dungeon exploration and provide a satisfying sense of accomplishment when overcome. From a presentation standpoint, DUNGEON SLASHER succeeds in delivering a cohesive identity. Its colorful pixel graphics are expressive without becoming overly detailed, ensuring that the action remains readable even during chaotic moments. Character animations are fluid, spell effects carry enough visual impact to feel rewarding, and the soundtrack complements the game's energetic pace. While some areas and enemy types eventually begin to repeat, the consistent art direction helps maintain the game's charm across extended play sessions. That said, the game is not without shortcomings. As with many roguelikes, the reliance on repetition can become a barrier for players who prefer narrative-driven experiences or a stronger sense of progression between runs. Certain skill combinations feel noticeably more effective than others, leading to occasional balance concerns that can diminish the incentive to experiment. Additionally, the minimalist approach to storytelling means that the focus remains almost entirely on gameplay, which may leave some players wanting greater context for the world and its characters. Despite these issues, DUNGEON SLASHER delivers exactly what it promises: an accessible and highly replayable action roguelike built around satisfying combat and endless build possibilities. It understands its audience and rarely strays from its core strengths. For players who enjoy refining strategies, discovering overpowered combinations, and tackling increasingly difficult challenges, it offers an addictive gameplay loop that is difficult to walk away from. It may not redefine the genre, but it confidently stands as an enjoyable and polished entry that demonstrates a clear understanding of what makes roguelikes so compelling. Rating: 6/10

Here's my review based on my own personal experience after hours of gameplay on the mobile version The game has several flaws: + Hard to start, early game is hell, takes time to understand and can easily get boring + Repetitive gameplay, dungeons after dungeons, same every time, that's the only way to get stronger, there are other gamemodes but they arent very unique on their own + Shop pricing, the prices are just too high, it's not worth buying anything at all, you even need to pay to get rid of the ads locking your items in the dungeon if you want an easier life + Save game, you have to finish a floor in order to temporily save your progress in that dungeon, sadly there's no other way + The setting, it's very basic, not much to do with it, they couldve make the UI better though + Events, each events last for around a month or more, yeah it takes a huge amount of time to get all the rewards But yeah we should talk about what's good about this game too + The design, characters are gorgeous, weapons are captivating, skills and items too, personally I like the artstyle and that pixelated design + Bosses are good, theyre dang strong, which gives motivation to continue growing in the game + Secrets, there's a lot of hidden places to explore + The concept, It's hard to find this kind of game nowadays + Game mechanics, a lot to learn, a lot to explore, again, hard to understand but once you do, the game becomes very enjoyable + Character development, abilities and weapons, each character has their own unique pros and cons, no one is perfect, you can choose your own secret abilities once you reach level 30, which is kinda cool There are two things i feel neutral about though + The lore, or rather, the tutorial, maybe having a bit more stories wouldve made this game a lot more enjoyable + Music, lobby ost might be the best ost out of all the music in the game, despite that they all are just too short and repetitive. The experience couldve improved a lot by just making better ost for the game Also by the time of this writing, the steam version got a bug, every time you enter the mimic in the arena and move to the right, the game would crash, and the progress would not be saved, keep that in mind, this will very likely be fixed in the future though given that the game just got released 3 days ago. Edit: Yeah this is fixed now Overall, give this game a try and see if it suits your taste, some bad reviews should not be the reason keeping you away from an experience
